The upper end of the power supply is connected to the top node of the bridge, and the lower end of the power supply is connected to the bottom node of the bridge; the bottom node is grounded. The left branch of the bridge is composed of R1 above and R2 below connected in series, and the middle node is labeled a; the right branch is composed of R4 above and R3 below connected in series, and the middle node is labeled b. An ideal voltmeter is connected between a and b, and the polarity of the voltmeter in the figure is that the a end is positive and the b end is negative. Reasoning: The internal resistance of an ideal voltmeter is infinite, so the voltmeter branch is open-circuited and does not affect the two left and right voltage-divider branches. Take the bottom ground point as 0 V, and the top node as +10 V. Given R1=R2=R4=R, R3=1.1R. In the left branch, point a is the voltage-divider point of R1 and R2, so Va = 10 * R2/(R1+R2) = 10 * R/(R+R) = 5 V.
